nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a formula of first-order logic with least fixed points, whose relation symbols are natural numbers. All fixed points of $\varphi$ are positive when every least-fixed-point subformula of $\varphi$, nested ones included, binds a relation symbol $R \ge 2$ (so neither the order symbol $0$ nor the edge symbol $1$) and $R$ occurs only positively in the body of that subformula.
nodes.title: Formulas whose fixed points are all positive

nodes.summary: Source: N. Immerman, "Relational queries definable in polynomial time", Information and Control 68 (1986), 193-243 (STOC 1983); M. Y. Vardi, "The complexity of relational query languages", Proceedings of the Fourteenth Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC 1982), 137-146.
nodes.title: Immerman-Vardi: FO + least fixed point is P on ordered structures

nodes.summary: A relation symbol $R$ occurs only negatively in a formula $\varphi$ of first-order logic with least fixed points when every atomic formula $R(x_{a_1}, \dots, x_{a_k})$ in $\varphi$, including those inside least-fixed-point subformulas, lies under an odd number of negations.
nodes.title: Negative occurrence of a relation symbol

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an ordered graph with vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$ and let $(E_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be predicates on lists of vertices. Relation symbol $0$ holds of a list exactly when it is a pair $(a, b)$ with $a < b$, relation symbol $1$ holds of a list exactly when it is a pair $(a, b)$ with an edge from $a$ to $b$ in $G$, and relation symbol $i + 2$ is interpreted as $E_i$.
nodes.title: Interpretation of relation symbols in an ordered graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an ordered graph with vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$ and edge table $t$, a list of booleans. There is an edge from $a$ to $b$ when the entry of $t$ at position $a n + b$ is true; positions beyond the end of $t$ count as false.
nodes.title: Edge relation of an ordered graph

nodes.summary: For a class $K$ of ordered graphs, this is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of pairs of a natural number and a list of booleans, to some $G \in K$ whose edge table has length exactly $n^2$, where $n$ is the number of vertices of $G$.
nodes.title: Encodings of a class of ordered graphs

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an ordered graph with vertex set $V = \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, let $\rho$ assign a vertex to each variable $0, 1, 2, \dots$, and let $S$ assign to each relation symbol $i$ a predicate $S_i$ on lists of vertices. The truth of a formula is defined by recursion: $x_a = x_b$ holds when $\rho(a) = \rho(b)$; the atom $R_i(x_{a_1}, \dots, x_{a_k})$ holds when $S_i$ holds of $(\rho(a_1), \dots, \rho(a_k))$;…
nodes.title: Evaluation of FO + LFP formulas in an ordered graph

nodes.summary: A class $K$ of ordered graphs is definable in first-order logic with least fixed points when there are a formula $\varphi$ and a boolean $b$ such that every ordered graph $G$ with $n$ vertices whose edge table has length $n^2$ lies in $K$ exactly when either $n > 0$ and $G$ satisfies $\varphi$, or $n = 0$ and $b$ is true.
nodes.title: Definability in FO + LFP

nodes.summary: An ordered graph $G$ with $n > 0$ vertices satisfies a formula $\varphi$ of first-order logic with least fixed points when $\varphi$ is well-formed in the environment where no relation symbol is bound, all fixed points of $\varphi$ are positive, and $\varphi$ is true in $G$ with every variable assigned the vertex $0$, relation symbol $0$ interpreted as the order $<$, relation symbol $1$ as the edge relation, and…
nodes.title: Satisfaction of an FO + LFP formula by an ordered graph

nodes.summary: Variables and relation symbols are natural numbers. Formulas are built from equalities $x_a = x_b$ and atoms $R_i(x_{a_1}, \dots, x_{a_k})$ by negation, conjunction, disjunction, existential quantification and least-fixed-point formulas $\mathrm{lfp}(R, k, \varphi, (a_1, \dots, a_m))$, the least fixed point of the operator defined by $\varphi$ (with $R$ as the recursive relation, of arity $k$) applied to the tuple…
nodes.title: Formulas of first-order logic with least fixed points

nodes.summary: Let $e$ assign to each relation symbol (a natural number) either an arity or nothing. Whether a first-order formula with least fixed points over ordered graphs is well-formed relative to $e$ is defined by recursion on the formula. An equality of two variables is well-formed. An atomic formula $R(x_1, \dots, x_k)$ is well-formed when $k = a$ if $e(R) = a$; when $k = 2$ if $e$ assigns nothing to $R$ and $R$ is $0$…
nodes.title: Well-formed FO + LFP formulas

nodes.summary: A finite ordered graph is a pair $(n, t)$ of a natural number $n$ and a finite list $t$ of booleans of any length. Here $n$ is the size of the domain $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, ordered numerically, and $t$ is read as a row-major edge table.
nodes.title: Finite ordered graphs

nodes.summary: A relation symbol $R$ occurs only positively in a first-order formula with least fixed points over ordered graphs when every atomic formula with relation symbol $R$ in it, including those inside least-fixed-point subformulas whatever symbol they bind, lies under an even number of negations.
nodes.title: Positive occurrence of a relation symbol

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
